title: The fakes
bridge: The three fakes are like MSW handlers for the backend: small real stand-ins that keep state and answer like the real service. Except: each fake sits behind the real interface (a real gRPC socket, the real storage base class, the real Celery send path). And each one has a contract suite that runs the same checks against the real client, MinIO or a Celery worker.
intro: The cloud talks to three things a test cannot run: on-prem clients over gRPC, an object store and Celery workers. This lesson builds the three fakes that replace mocks in tests_api/, one ticket each. It also builds the contract suites that keep them honest. It is Python because the code it stands in for is fcp's Django backend.

picture.caption: Cloud code under test reaches each fake through its real seam; a contract suite checks each fake against the real thing.

steps.text: calls an endpoint through the API client
AgentRpcClient sends real protobuf bytes over a real socket
StorageService builds the provider, and the fixture hands it the fake
apply_async ends in app.send_task, which the fixture replaced
calls drain() when it wants the tasks to run, oldest first
runs the same checks against the real services, in CI and in FCP Lab

p: Lesson p10-4 taught the idea. A fake is a small real implementation behind the real interface, swapped in at the seam and pinned by a contract suite. G7 applies it three times. Each fake replaces mocks counted in G7-01: 69 on AgentRpcClient, 24 on StorageService, 11 eager Celery classes.

The fakes live in tests_api/fakes/, one module each. Their fixtures live in tests_api/conftest.py: onprem_client, object_store and task_queue. The contract suites live in tests_api/contracts/ and carry the contract marker, so pytest tests_api -m contract runs only them.
Leave the existing mocks in rhinoCore/tests alone. New tests in tests_api use the fakes; old tests move only when someone ports them (lesson g7-3).

callout.text: The fakes are Python because they stand in for parts of fcp's Django backend and run inside its pytest process. The TypeScript platform never imports them.

p: The cloud reaches every Rhino client through one proxy gRPC service, RhinoCloudInternalRpcProxy. Its one method, AgentRpc, carries the agent id, a method name such as HealthCheck, and the request as protobuf bytes. AgentRpcClient wraps that call in cloud code.

The fake subclasses the generated servicer. So cloud code under test goes through the real AgentRpcClient, the real encoding and a real socket. A mock skips all three, which is where the 69 mocks drift.
sections.because: We subclass the generated servicer and use the real method table, because the fake must accept what the real proxy accepts.

code.text:
from fcp_common.rhinoAgentRpc import agent_rpc_onprem_side_pb2 as onprem
from fcp_common.rhinoAgentRpc.agent_rpc_internal_cloud_proxy_pb2 import AgentRpcResponse
from fcp_common.rhinoAgentRpc.agent_rpc_internal_cloud_proxy_pb2_grpc import RhinoCloudInternalRpcProxyServicer
from rhinoCloud.rhinoTaskServices.rhinoTaskResponseService.handle_task_response import handle_task_response

METHODS = onprem.RhinoAgentRpc.GetDescriptor().methods_by_name  # the same lookup AgentRpcClient uses


class FakeOnPremClient(RhinoCloudInternalRpcProxyServicer):
    """In-memory Rhino clients behind the real cloud->agent gRPC contract. Pinned by tests_api/contracts/ (also run on FCP Lab)."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.calls: list[tuple[str, str]] = []  # (rhino_agent_id, method_name)
        self.offline_agents: set[str] = set()
        self.scheduled: list[onprem.ScheduleTaskRequest] = []  # more handlers: SystemStatus, GetEnvironmentVariable, ...

sections.h: FakeOnPremClient, part 2: dispatch and finish a task
p: The fixture onprem_client starts grpc.server on 127.0.0.1:0; port 0 means any free port. It registers the fake with add_RhinoCloudInternalRpcProxyServicer_to_server. Then it monkeypatches AGENT_RPC_INTERNAL_CLOUD_PROXY_DNS and AGENT_RPC_INTERNAL_CLOUD_PROXY_PORT. AgentRpcClient reads those two settings every time it is created, so no production code changes.

The first scenarios need seven handlers: HealthCheck, SystemStatus, ScheduleTask, GetEnvironmentVariable, GetAgentGcpProjectId, ValidateDatasetImportPaths and GetTensorBoardLogsMetadata. The sketch shows two; the rest follow the same shape.
sections.because: We return an error that names a missing method, because a quiet default would let a test pass on an unbuilt path.

sections.h: InMemoryStorageProvider, part 1: a dict shaped like S3 (G7-05)
p: StorageService in rhinoCore/services/cloud_services/storage_service.py picks a provider class. When CLOUD_PROVIDER is AWS, which it is in the test env, its __init__ builds AWSStorageServiceProvider() at call time. The fixture object_store replaces that name: monkeypatch.setattr(storage_service, "AWSStorageServiceProvider", lambda: store). Production code does not change.

The fake implements every abstract method of CloudStorageServiceProviderBase, plus upload_file_from_bytes and storage_service_prefix. A bucket is a dict from object key to (bytes, last-modified time).
sections.because: We let a missing bucket raise, because the real store raises too and the contract suite pins that behaviour.

So the fixture also patches storage_service.requests.get to answer for http://object-store.fake from memory. That is the one extra seam, and the fake's docstring says so.

sections.h: FakeTaskQueue, part 1: record through the real serializer (G7-07)
p: CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER runs a task inside the caller at send time. Celery's docs say it is not suitable for testing: nothing waits in a queue, so order and timing differ from production. The fake records instead. Nothing runs until the test calls drain().

The seam is app.send_task on the app in rhinoCore/celery_tasks/app.py. Task.apply_async ends in that method, so RhinoTask's header injection still runs before the fake sees the task. The fixture does monkeypatch.setattr(app, "send_task", queue.send_task).
sections.because: We push the arguments through kombu's dumps and loads, because an argument a broker cannot carry must fail in the test.

code.text:
import uuid
from collections import namedtuple

from celery.canvas import maybe_signature
from kombu.serialization import dumps, loads

from rhinoCloud.rhinoCore.celery_tasks.app import app

SentTask = namedtuple("SentTask", "name args kwargs options task_id")


class FakeTaskQueue:
    """Stands in for the broker: send_task() records, drain() runs, oldest first. Unlike CELERY_TASK_ALWAYS_EAGER,
    arguments go through our serializer (pickle) as on Redis, and nothing runs until the test asks."""

    def __init__(self):
        self.sent: list[SentTask] = []
        self.ran: list[SentTask] = []

    def send_task(self, name, args=None, kwargs=None, task_id=None, **options):  # replaces app.send_task
        content_type, encoding, body = dumps((args or (), kwargs or {}), serializer=app.conf.task_serializer)
        args, kwargs = loads(body, content_type, encoding, accept=app.conf.accept_content)
        self.sent.append(SentTask(name, tuple(args), kwargs, options, task_id or str(uuid.uuid4())))
        return app.AsyncResult(self.sent[-1].task_id)  # callers read .id; tests call drain(), never .get()

callout.text: In this lesson's lab, kombu's loads refused accept=["json"] with ContentDisallowed: it wants content types such as application/json. If fcp's accept_content lists names like pickle and json, wrap it: accept=prepare_accept_content(app.conf.accept_content), imported from kombu.serialization.

sections.h: FakeTaskQueue, part 2: drain, errors and chains
p: drain() runs the recorded tasks in-process with Task.apply. A chain is a list of tasks where each one starts after the previous finished and gets its result. Celery stores the rest of a chain in the chain option, reversed, so the next task is the last entry. vocabulary_indexing.index_large_vocabulary and the NVFlare inference flow use chains.
sections.because: We re-raise each task's own error in the test, because a swallowed exception would turn a broken task into a green test.

notes.text: Run everything that was sent, including tasks sent by the tasks themselves.
Loop until the queue is empty; a chain adds new entries while we drain.
Take the oldest task first, like a queue.
Run the registered task in this process with its args, id and recorded headers. RhinoTask restores its metadata context from the headers.
Raise the task's own exception here, in the test.
The walrus operator assigns and tests in one step: is there a chain to continue?
The next task is the last entry, because Celery keeps the rest of a chain reversed.
Send it the normal way, which lands in our send_task again. An immutable signature takes no result; otherwise pass the previous result.
Remember the order the tasks ran in.

sections.h: Contract suites in CI and in the Lab
p: Each fake gets a contract file in tests_api/contracts/ with the contract marker. The on-prem one checks a health call, an unknown agent id, a scheduled task with its response, and the timeout error type. The task-queue one checks a plain task, a chain, an error and the metadata context kept.

The real sides need real services. MinIO (public.ecr.aws/u7h0g2s9/rhinofcp/minio:2025.2.7) and Redis (public.ecr.aws/u7h0g2s9/rhinofcp/redis:7.4.3) join the API Tests job as services. They are the same images the test job uses, and the job runs pytest tests_api -m contract. The Celery side starts a worker with celery.contrib.testing.worker.start_worker. It needs a transactional database, because results go to the django-db result backend.

The on-prem suite has a --target option: fake by default, lab against FCP Lab. With lab, the proxy settings point at the Lab's agent-rpc-cloud-side-service and the Lab's client id. Lesson g7-6 (G7-26) runs it there.

callout.text: RQ jobs such as task_response_job are not in FakeTaskQueue's scope. FakeOnPremClient.complete_task reaches that code directly instead. Note too: in the lab, Celery 5.6.3 eager mode also refused an argument JSON cannot carry. Check fcp's pinned Celery version before you repeat the serialization argument; the order argument holds either way.

import pytest
from celery.contrib.testing.worker import start_worker

from fake_queue import FakeTaskQueue
from tasks import app


@pytest.fixture(params=["fake", "real"])
def queue(request, monkeypatch):
    if request.param == "fake":
        fake = FakeTaskQueue()
        monkeypatch.setattr(app, "send_task", fake.send_task)
        yield lambda results: fake.drain()
    else:
        with start_worker(app, perform_ping_check=False):
            yield lambda results: [r.get(timeout=10) for r in results]

Create tests/test_queue_contract.py, the contract suite:

import pytest
from kombu.exceptions import EncodeError

from tasks import add


def test_a_task_returns_its_result(queue):
    results = [add.delay(2, 3), add.delay(10, 1)]
    assert queue(results) == [5, 11]


def test_an_argument_json_cannot_carry_fails_at_send_time(queue):
    with pytest.raises(EncodeError):
        add.delay({1, 2}, 3)

quiz.q: Why do FakeOnPremClient's handlers never write to the database?

options.text: Because the fake has no Django settings loaded.
options.why: It runs inside the same pytest process with the same settings.

options.text: Because they run on a gRPC server thread, outside the test's transaction.
options.why: Rows written there would not be rolled back with the test; complete_task() runs on the test's own thread instead.

options.text: Because the real client also never writes to the cloud database.
options.why: True, but that is not the reason; the thread and transaction are.

quiz.q: A test marks an agent as offline and calls an endpoint that health-checks it. What does the fake return?

options.text: It raises a Python exception in the view.
options.why: The real proxy does not raise; it answers with an error type, and the fake does the same.
That would hide the offline case; the agent is in offline_agents.

options.text: An AgentRpcResponse with error_type TIMEOUT, as the real proxy answers for a client that is not connected.
options.why: The contract suite pins this error type against FCP Lab too.

quiz.q: Why does FakeTaskQueue.send_task serialize and deserialize the arguments?

options.text: So an argument the broker could not carry fails in the test, as it would on Redis.
options.why: That is the point of recording through the real serializer.

options.text: Because Task.apply requires bytes as input.
options.why: apply takes Python args and kwargs; the round trip is our choice.

options.text: To copy the arguments so later changes in the test cannot affect them.
options.why: A side effect at most; the reason is to behave like the broker.
